articles.title: At Daisy Chain Fields, Olivia Rodrigo, Chappell Roan and Honored Forebears Convene for a Superb Festival That’s Hot to Go in Every Way: Concert Review
articles.summary: You know an inaugural festival has been a success when, after the temperature reached 95 degrees, humidity topped 80%… perspiration stains were so pervasive that it was the odd dry spots that looked like stains… constant 12-minute trudges back and forth between two action-packed stages threatened…
body: Elder stateswomen ranging from the Breeders and Bikini Kill to Sarah McLachlan and Stevie Nicks were a key part of an event that offered contemporary lights as different and excellent as Doechii and Mitski back to back.

Now if they could just find a way to schedule future editions of the festival at a more meteorologically reasonable time, some period of the year where it is reliably warm in SoCal yet not prone to insanely long heat waves, because climate change has abated and… well, never mind, fine … August probably is as good a time as any.

What a distraction from all that the 14-act bill (plus three guest stars) managed to provide over a 10-and-a-half-hour day of music, with one killer act after another representing a wide gamut of styles and eras, bearing a sold amount of diversity except for the lone common-denominator criterion for booking.

body: “Kristen is one of the best in the business and we stand by her,” NBC News said in a statement Sunday afternoon. Welker did not utter any of the remarks that angered Trump during NBC’s actual broadcast of “Meet the Press” on Sunday.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo Raises $20 Million With Daisy Chain Fields Festival Thanks to Matching Commitment From Melinda French Gates
articles.summary: Olivia Rodrigo raised a significant sum of $10 million with her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Festival — and then doubled it to $20 million, thanks to a matching commitment from philanthropist Melinda French Gates.
body: Gates joined Rodrigo on stage to commend her for her philanthropic efforts with Daisy Chain Fields. “ Olivia Rodrigo is a force,” said French Gates. “What Daisy Chain Fields sets in motion will last far beyond a single night, by opening up opportunity for women and girls around the world and showing a new generation how much their voices matter. I’m so proud to support Olivia’s vision.”

The $20 million will be distributed equally across 10 different nonprofit organizations supporting women and girls. Among the organizations are Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeForm, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center and Planned Parenthood.

At the festival, attendees enjoyed performances from a slew of performers that also included Bikini Kill, Eli, Mitski, Not for Radio, Rachel Chinouriri, Santigold, the Breeders and more. Throughout the day, concertgoers were encouraged to learn about the nonprofits through Daisy Chain Reaction, which offered information about the causes.

articles.title: Katseye’s Sophia to Sit Out European Leg of ‘Wildworld’ Tour to ‘Focus on Her Well-Being’
articles.summary: Katseye member Sophia Laforteza will not be joining the group for the U.K. and European dates of their upcoming “Wildworld” tour, which is scheduled to launch on Tuesday.
body: This marks yet another wrinkle for Katseye, which has had a series of swings throughout the year. In February, just after they performed at the Grammys, member Manon Bannerman announced that she would be taking a temporary hiatus from Katseye to “focus on her health and wellbeing.” Earlier this month, Laforteza announced that she would be following suit so that she could prioritize her “mental health and wellness.” Then, just days before Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival, where they were slated to perform, the group dropped out of the lineup, citing member Megan Skiendiel’s ankle injury as the reason for their absence.

Amid it all, Katseye has continued to soar as a pop force, earning their first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 with “Wild” in August. The “Wildworld” tour is slated to kick off on Tuesday at Dublin’s 3Arena, with stops planned for Paris, Amsterdam and Copenhagen. Katseye will head back to the States for an extensive leg in North America beginning on October 13 at Miami’s Kaseya Center.

articles.title: Big tech goes to Hollywood: is Silicon Valley ready for a silver-screen reckoning?
articles.summary: Its moguls are ripe subjects for drama, and there is huge anticipation for forthcoming features The Social Reckoning and Artificial. But other projects have failed as the film industry is increasingly colonised by IT empires.
body: ‘I know there are easier enemies to make,” tech reporter Jeremy Allen White tells his colleague in a recent trailer for The Social Reckoning. “The mafia would be an easier enemy to make,” comes the reply. They’re talking about Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta, but they might as well be discussing big tech as a whole. As The Social Reckoning promises to underline, it’s become clear that these people are not on our side – “us” being the whole of humanity except billionaire tech overlords and their mates. But for an industry that loves a clear-cut baddie, Hollywood has barely landed a blow on the tech industry. Now it finds itself in mortal danger of being absorbed by it. Is it too late to fight back?

articles.title: Why Owner of ‘Heated Rivalry’ Cottage Did Some “Soul Searching” Before Agreeing to Season 2
articles.summary: The now-famous cottage served as the emotional backdrop for a major turning point in the queer hockey romance show's first season, which starred Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie.
body: The owner of the cottage made famous in Heated Rivalry season one says he needed to do some “soul searching” before allowing production to return for season two.

During a recent interview with HGTV, Michael Kutryk revealed that he was contacted about filming for the highly anticipated second season, which got underway earlier this month. However, he said it wasn’t an immediate yes.

In season one of HBO Max and Crave’s breakout queer hockey romance, the cottage served as the emotional backdrop for a major turning point. When Shane Hollander (Hudson Williams) invited his secret lover, Ilya Rozanov (Connor Storrie), to his private cottage for a two-week stay of uninterrupted alone time together, it led to them growing closer and ultimately confessing their love for each other. But the cottage also played a role in Ilya and Shane deciding to come out to the latter’s parents after Shane’s father accidentally caught them together at the home.

articles.title: 10 Best '70s Movies That Could Never Be Made Today
articles.summary: Plenty of films in the 1970s challenged audiences with provocative material, and even though these movies are revered now, they'd never be made today.
body: Here are 10 movies from the 1970s that couldn't be made today.

"Deliverance" features the kind of pensive, shocking, and dark subject matter that major studios don't pursue as heavily today, and its production was dangerous as all get out. The story of four civilized men from the city who seek to canoe down the rapids of a soon-to-be-dammed river and come face-to-face with the random violence and savagery of the natural world was shot on location in Rabun County, Georgia, and you can feel the real-life peril of the actors performing dangerous in-camera stunts.

Warner Bros. was already nervous about the John Boorman-directed film's thematic content during production, and they slashed the budget. That led the main performers to do it themselves: Jon Voight got shots of him actually free-climbing the cliffside, Burt Reynolds wanted a go at being in one of the canoes as it went over a waterfall, and Ned Beatty nearly drowned while shooting other footage of the rapids. A huge fistfight also broke out on set, though that was more of an occupational hazard related to stubborn creatives than dying at the hands of nature.
points: Plenty of films in the 1970s challenged audiences with provocative material, and even though these movies are revered now, they'd never be made today.

articles.title: The Best Star Trek Books Ever Should Have Been Adapted Into A TV Series
articles.summary: The world of Star Trek has been expanded in many mediums, and the best series of books would have made for a great TV series.
body: The 1990s were a great time to be a Trekkie. "Star Trek: The Next Generation" was riding high in 1993 when "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine" debuted, and the two shows ran concurrently for a spell. "Next Generation" had its seventh season finale in May of 1994 before moving to the big screen with "Star Trek: Generations" the following November. In January of 1995, "Star Trek: Voyager" premiered, and in 1996 and 1998, there were two more "Next Generation"-based movies. "Deep Space Nine" and "Voyager" ran for a crackerjack seven seasons apiece, leaving the air in 1999 and 2001, respectively. The air was thick with Trek, and the possibilities seemed endless.

In the middle of all this, in 1997, there was even a "Star Trek" spinoff that few people — other than the staunchest of Trekkies — really took notice of. The legendary Marvel comic book author and widely celebrated "Star Trek" tie-in novelist Peter David invented an entirely new "Star Trek" ship, stocked it with its own raft of characters, and sent it on its own continuing mission, all to be experienced in a long-running series of books called "Star Trek: New Frontier."
points: The world of Star Trek has been expanded in many mediums, and the best series of books would have made for a great TV series.
